fcmTokens._comment: One entry per device that's enabled push notifications — key is either the signed-in user's uid or a generated anonymous device id (see getOrCreateDeviceId() in index.html), value is that device's current FCM token. Read access is intentionally admin-only (a token is effectively a way to push notifications AT that specific device, so it shouldn't be publicly listable) — /api/send-notification.js reads this list using a plain unauthenticated fetch because it runs server-side with its own trusted context, not through this client-facing rule.

notifiedReleases._comment: Written by api/cron-check-releases.js (the daily automatic new-release checker) to remember which TMDB movie ids it has already sent a push for, so the next day's run doesn't notify the same release twice. Read/write only via the cron job's own service-account-signed request (see that file) — no client code ever touches this path, so it stays admin-only here purely as a safe default, matching every other server-managed tree in this file.

adAnalytics._comment: Written by ads-engine.js from EVERY page that shows ads, including the standalone Privacy Policy and Terms of Service pages — those pages don't run Firebase Auth at all (no sign-in flow, no anonymous auth), so this intentionally allows unauthenticated writes, unlike every other write path in this app. Scoped narrowly (append-only child pushes under 'loads'/'errors' only, never any read) so the worst a bad actor could do is push junk log entries — they can never read anyone's data or affect any other part of the app through this path.
